title: The Bulaq Boys
teaser: A street team, a broken ball and a poster on a wall.
paragraphs: In Bulaq, near the Nile, there is a small street team. They have no coach and no real pitch. They play between parked cars with a ball that is losing air. The captain is Tarek, fifteen years old, fast and loud.
One evening, Tarek sees a new poster on the wall of the bakery. “Youth Cup for Neighbourhood Teams. Winner plays in a real stadium. Teams of seven. Registration: 500 pounds.”

Tarek reads it three times. Then he runs to his friends. “We are going to play in a stadium!” he shouts. His friends laugh. “With what money?” asks Bebo, the goalkeeper. “And we are only five players.”
Tarek looks at the old ball, the parked cars and his five friends. He knows it is crazy. But he also knows that this is the chance they always wanted.

“Give me one week,” he says. “I will find the money and two more players.” That night, he cannot sleep. He has a plan, but it is a dangerous one: he needs help from the one person in Bulaq who never helps anyone, old Am Shawky.

title: The Bulaq Boys
teaser: Nobody visits Am Shawky. Tarek knocks on his door.
paragraphs: Am Shawky lives alone on the top floor of the oldest building in the street. Children are afraid of him. He never smiles, and when their ball hits his window, he shouts for ten minutes.
But Tarek has heard a story from his grandmother. Forty years ago, Shawky was a famous player in the neighbourhood. People called him “the Wall”. Then he hurt his knee, and he never played again.
Tarek climbs the stairs and knocks. The door opens a little. “What do you want?” says a deep voice. Tarek takes a breath. “We need a coach. And… we need 500 pounds.”
Am Shawky starts to close the door. Tarek puts his foot in it. “My grandmother says you were the best defender in Bulaq. She says you could read the game like a book.”

There is a long silence. Then the door opens fully. Am Shawky looks at Tarek for a long time. “Bring your team tomorrow at six in the morning,” he says. “If one of you is late, I am finished with you.” The door closes. Tarek runs down the stairs, jumping three steps at a time.

title: The Bulaq Boys
teaser: No ball for three days. Am Shawky has a strange way of training.
paragraphs: At six in the morning, five sleepy boys stand in the street. Am Shawky arrives with a stick and a bag of plastic cones. He does not say good morning. He says, “Run.”

For three days, there is no ball. They run, jump and pass imaginary balls. They practise standing in the right place. Bebo complains, “This is not football!” Am Shawky answers, “Football is ninety percent thinking and running. The ball is the easy part.”
On the fourth day, Am Shawky brings a new ball. The boys look at it like it is gold. “Where did you get it?” asks Tarek. The old man shrugs. “I had some money under my bed. Doing nothing.”

He also solves the second problem. He brings two new players: his grandnephew Hamada, who is very tall, and a quiet girl from the next street called Rahma. “She is the fastest player in Bulaq,” says Am Shawky. The boys are surprised, but after five minutes, nobody can catch her.

Now they are seven. But they still need 500 pounds for the registration. The deadline is in four days. That evening, Rahma has an idea. “My mother makes the best basbousa in Cairo,” she says. “What if we sell it?”

title: The Bulaq Boys
teaser: Basbousa, a rainy afternoon and a very big problem.
paragraphs: Rahma’s mother agrees to help, but only if the team helps her in the kitchen. So for two days, seven football players mix flour, sugar and yoghurt. Bebo eats more basbousa than he cuts.

On Friday after prayer, they put a table outside the mosque. They write a sign: “Basbousa for the Bulaq Team – Help Us Play in a Stadium!” People are curious. The baker buys ten pieces. Grandmothers buy for their grandchildren.
By three o’clock, they have 420 pounds. They need only 80 more. Then dark clouds come over the Nile, and it starts to rain heavily. Everyone runs home. The street is empty.
The team stands under a balcony, wet and sad. Tomorrow is the deadline. Tarek counts the money again. Still 420. “It’s over,” says Hamada.

Then a window opens above them. It is Am Shawky. He looks down at the wet children and the unsold basbousa. He says nothing. A few minutes later, he comes down with an umbrella, buys all the basbousa that is left, and puts 80 pounds on the table. “I am hungry,” he says, and walks back home.

title: The Bulaq Boys
teaser: Their first match is against the team from the rich club. Everyone expects a disaster.
paragraphs: The tournament starts on a real pitch with green grass and white lines. The Bulaq team has no matching shirts, so Am Shawky buys seven white T-shirts and writes numbers on them with a black marker.

Their first opponent is the team from a rich sports club. They have expensive boots, a coach with a tablet and a bus with their name on it. Some of their players laugh at the T-shirts. Bebo feels small. Even Tarek is nervous.

Before the match, Am Shawky calls them together. “They have better boots,” he says. “But you have played between cars for years. You know how to play in small spaces. Keep the ball on the ground. Pass fast. And Rahma… run.”

At half-time, it is 1–0 to the club team. In the second half, Tarek remembers the training without a ball. He stops looking at the ball and starts looking for space. He sees Rahma running. He passes, and she scores. 1–1.

With one minute left, the club’s striker shoots hard. Bebo jumps higher than ever and catches it. He kicks it long to Hamada, who heads it to Tarek. Tarek shoots. Goal! 2–1. The small group of people from Bulaq goes crazy. On the bench, Am Shawky is smiling for the first time in years.

title: The Bulaq Boys
teaser: The final. A real stadium. And a promise Tarek must keep.
paragraphs: The Bulaq team wins two more matches. Now they are in the final, and the final is in a real stadium, just like the poster said. The whole street comes by microbus. The baker brings a drum. Rahma’s mother brings basbousa for everyone.
The other team is very strong. They score in the first five minutes, and again before half-time. 2–0. In the changing room, nobody speaks. Bebo has tears in his eyes.

Am Shawky stands up slowly. “Forty years ago,” he says, “I played my last match in this stadium. I hurt my knee, and I stopped. I stopped everything. I stopped playing, stopped smiling, stopped talking to people.” He looks at each of them. “Don’t stop. Whatever the score.”

In the second half, they play the best football of their lives. Hamada scores with his head. 2–1. Then, in the last minute, Tarek is pushed in the box. Penalty. He takes the ball, but he looks at the bench. He walks to Am Shawky and gives him the ball. “You take it,” he says. “It is your stadium too.”

The referee does not allow it, of course. So Tarek takes the penalty himself. He misses. They lose 2–1. But when the final whistle blows, the people from Bulaq are singing. Am Shawky hugs every player. On Monday morning at six, the whole team is waiting in the street. They are not late. And this time, the old man brings two balls.
